recipes.name: Strawberry Salad Dessert
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.25 ounce) package angel food cake mix
1 (12 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) with oven rack in lowest position.
Beat cake mix and 1 ¼ cups cold water in a bowl using an electric mixer on low speed until moistened, about 30 seconds. Beat on medium speed for 1 minute. Pour into an ungreased angel food tube pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is golden brown and cracked, looks very dry and firm to the touch, 33 to 38 minutes.

Cool cake in the pan, inverted onto a wire rack, empty wine bottle, or thin-necked glass bottle; this will prevent the cake from sinking, about 1 ½ hours. Loosen edges with a flat knife or a spatula to remove cake. Trim crust from cake; save for another use. Cut cake into cubes, or tear into bite-sized chunks; set aside.

Combine boiling water and gelatin in a large bowl; stir until gelatin is dissolved. Stir in frozen strawberries and remaining 1 cup cold water. Chill until slightly thickened to the consistency of egg whites; it may reach this stage while stirring.
Gently fold cake cubes and whipped topping into strawberry mixture. Chill until set, about 2 hours. Decorate top with any remaining strawberries and whipped topping.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Salad Dessert
raw_recipe.description: This strawberry salad dessert recipe is an easy, refreshing, cool gelatin treat made with angel food cake, whipped topping, and frozen strawberries.

review.reviewBody: Great for Valentines Day! The recipe is alot quicker if you use a ready made angel food cake. I let it chill in a 13 x 9 pan and garnish it with sliced strawberries. It slices easily, so next time, I might use large cookie cutters in the shape of hearts to serve. It's really good -- everyone loved it.

Delightfully simple, light, and delicious! Made it to take to work; forgot to get a pic until there was only a little left...:) Like some of the other commentators, I waited till the Jello mixture (using less water) was the consistency of egg whites. Folded in the cool whip and then the cake cubes; put it in a 9x13” pan, spread a little more cool whip over top and garnished with fresh strawberries (sliced). Everyone at work loved it!

This dessert is similar to those poke cakes, the kind where you pierce a 13"x9" cake with a skewer and pour liquid Jell-O over the top, then frost it with Cool Whip, EXCEPT it's quicker to assemble. It came out perfectly even though I used sugar-free Jell-O, Cool Whip Lite, a store-bought angel food cake, and made individual servings in dessert glasses. This is a perfect dessert to make when you need something sweet but light on a sweltering August day.

I used fresh strawberries instead of frozen and used an angel food cake already made from the bakery. This dessert was fantastic! Make sure you let the jello combo gel up fairly well so you don't end up with mushy angel food cake. Will make this again in the summer as it is light and fluffy. Loved it!

My family really love the flavor and the lightness of those dish. I loved the ease of preparation (I used a pre-made angel food cake). My only complaint is that most of the cake cubes completely dissolved into the liquid, whereas I would have preferred more chunks of cake. Next time, I think I will reserve some of the cake cubes and fold them in right before serving.
This is what I am always ask to bring to family dinners. I use sugar free jello and lite cool whip always a hit

I lost my old recipe and I was so happy to find this recipe. I was a perfect light dessert for our Valentine's Prime Rib dinner. I did use fresh strawberries but the rest was perfect just as written. Thank you so much for replacing my old missing yummy recipe.
My grandmother started making this about 35 years ago. ..she also added a tiny can of crushed pineapple...yummy
It turned out exactly like it said.. I did use a little less water though. so it would set faster.. and I also used some strawberries of my own that i had frozen.. worked great.

I love this recipe! It's the same dessert my grandma used to make. Make sure you let the jello and strawberries get pretty jelled before adding the angel food cake. I buy the baked cake from the store instead of making my own.
Mine was way too soggy. I think the water could be cut back. Strawberries hold a lot of water. Anyway, I would not make this again and take the chance on it being that soggy.
This was absolutely delicious. I used regular white cake and cut it up into pieces. extremely easy to make and a joy to eat:)
Turned out awesome! I mixed cool whip into the jello.

I must have done something wrong with this. The angel food cake turned into mush even though I thought I had waited long enough to mix it in. Two different people said it looked like pink brains. Taste was ok, but the consistency with the mushed cake was not appealing.
it was awesome! I loved it....took to a family reunion and was GONE.....definitely a crowd pleaser in our family
